passages.text: Clinical and functional evidence supporting pathogenicity of a novel APOA5 variant in familial chylomicronemia syndrome
Objective
This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and functional impact of a novel apolipoprotein A5 (ApoA5) variant by assessing lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity.
Subjects and methods

Demographic and clinical data, including blood lipid levels and body mass index, were retrospectively collected from an endocrinology clinic registry. <sentence_start/>Ten individuals with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) carrying a novel <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant were included. <sentence_start/>Whole-exome sequencing was performed using the latest generation DNB-SEQ400 platform. <sentence_start/>LPL activity was measured in post-heparin plasma using a radiometric assay. <sentence_start/>Statistical analysis: Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies and percentages, and continuous variables as mean ± standard deviation or median (range), as appropriate. <sentence_start/>Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or chi-square test. <sentence_start/>Analyses were conducted using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences software (v. 25.0). <sentence_start/>A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results

We report ten cases of FCS with a homozygous missense variant of uncertain significance in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic>: c.694T>C; p.(Ser232Pro), located in exon 3. <sentence_start/>In six patients assessed for LPL activity, levels remained consistently below 20% compared to normotriglyceridemic controls. <sentence_start/>The addition of exogenous serum containing <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> restored LPL activity to above 20% in all cases, indicating functional rescue.
Conclusion

Measurement of LPL activity demonstrated the functional impact of the APOA5 c.694T>C; p.(Ser232Pro) variant. <sentence_start/>These findings support reclassification of the variant as likely pathogenic and enable differentiation from multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome.
INTRODUCTION

Apolipoprotein A5 (<italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic>) is a critical regulator of plasma triglyceride (TG) levels (<citation rid="r1" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2018.10.006" pmid="30466821" count="1"><sup>1</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>It modulates hepatic synthesis of very low-density lipoprotein (<citation rid="r2" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2011.07.019" pmid="21831376" count="1"><sup>2</sup></citation>), enhances lipoprotein lipase-mediated triglyceride clearance (<citation rid="r3" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1074/jbc.M403240200" pmid="15090553" count="1"><sup>3</sup></citation>), and promotes hepatic uptake of TG-rich lipoprotein remnants via the low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor family (<citation rid="r4" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1021/bi7000533" pmid="17326667" count="1"><sup>4</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic> enhances LPL activity through interactions with heparan sulfate proteoglycans (<citation rid="r5" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1074/jbc.M501589200" pmid="15878877" count="1"><sup>5</sup></citation>) and glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored high-density lipoprotein-binding protein 1 (<italic toggle="yes">Gpihbp1</italic>) on endothelial cell surfaces (<citation rid="r6" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1074/jbc.M802579200" pmid="18713736" pmcid="PMC2662032" count="1"><sup>6</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Biallelic loss-of-function (LOF) variants in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> underlie a rare condition with an estimated prevalence of 1-10 per million (<citation rid="r7" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1194/jlr.R009720" pmid="21041806" pmcid="PMC3023540" count="1"><sup>7</sup></citation>) and represent a known cause of familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) (<citation rid="r8" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1210/endrev/bnab037" pmid="34676866" pmcid="PMC9277652" count="1"><sup>8</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r9" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2023.08.003" pmid="37586912" count="1"><sup>9</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Even severely truncated <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variants are synthesized and secreted (<citation rid="r10" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1172/JCI24471" pmid="16200213" pmcid="PMC1236672" count="1"><sup>10</sup></citation>); however, premature truncation can disrupt key functional domains, leading to protein misfolding. <sentence_start/>In homozygous or compound heterozygous states, these alterations result in a significant reduction in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> mass and function (<citation rid="r11" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1097/01.mol.0000217892.00618.54" pmid="16531747" count="1"><sup>11</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r12" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1161/01.ATV.0000153087.36428.dd" pmid="15591215" count="1"><sup>12</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Only 38% of <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variants are classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic (<citation rid="r13" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2015.30" pmid="25741868" pmcid="PMC4544753" count="1"><sup>13</sup></citation>), most of which are missense mutations. <sentence_start/>When genetic testing yields negative or inconclusive results, measurement of LPL activity can confirm the diagnosis of FCS, particularly when activity is reduced below 20-25% of the normalmedian (<citation rid="r14" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2018.05.013" pmid="30318066" count="1"><sup>14</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r15" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2025.03.013" pmid="40234111" count="1"><sup>15</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>In this study, we describe the clinical and genetic characteristics of patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia carrying <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variants and assess their pathogenicity by measuring LPL activity in ten affected individuals.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS

Ten patients (3 men, 7 women; mean age: 42 ± 3.2 years) with strong clinical suspicion for FCS were included. <sentence_start/>Serum TG, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B were measured using commercial enzymatic assays on a Mindray BS360E autoanalyzer (Mindray, China). <sentence_start/>Body mass index and the Moulin score were calculated (<citation rid="r16" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2018.06.814" pmid="29980054" count="1"><sup>16</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Secondary causes of hypertriglyceridemia were excluded.
DNA preparation and sequencing

Peripheral blood samples were collected from all patients, and whole-exome sequencing was performed using the latest-generation DNB-SEQ400 platform. <sentence_start/>Genes associated with FCS (e.g., <italic toggle="yes">LPL</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">APOC2</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">GPIHBP1</italic>, and <italic toggle="yes">LMF1</italic>) were analyzed. <sentence_start/>High-quality reads were aligned to the human reference genome (GRCh37/hg19). <sentence_start/>The analysis focused on variants in exonic and splice-site regions (minimum 20 bp), as well as small insertions and deletions (copy number variants). <sentence_start/>Variant classification followed the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines (<citation rid="r13" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2015.30" pmid="25741868" pmcid="PMC4544753" count="1"><sup>13</sup></citation>), using the ClinGen framework (clinicalgenome.org). <sentence_start/>Databases consulted included Clinical Variation database, Human Gene Mutation Database, Leiden Open Variation Database, Database of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms, Genome Aggregation Database, and in-house resources. <sentence_start/>The identified variant exhibited extremely low allelic frequency in the general population (0.000002502 in gnomAD v. 4.1), consistent with a pathogenic allele in a recessive inheritance model. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">In silico</italic> prediction tools (REVEL, BayesDel) classified the variant as deleterious.
LPL activity

To assess LPL activity, heparin was administered intravenously at a dose of 60 IU/kg body weight. <sentence_start/>Ten minutes after injection, blood samples were collected from the contralateral arm into ice-chilled tubes. <sentence_start/>Post-heparin plasma was obtained by centrifugation at 1500 × g for 10 minutes at 4 °C and stored at -70 °C until analysis. <sentence_start/>LPL activity was measured in post-heparin plasma from six patients. <sentence_start/>A standardized LPL activity assay was developed in our laboratory based on the Nilsson-Ehle method (<citation rid="r17" ref-type="bibr" pmid="7033153" count="1"><sup>17</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r18" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1161/ATVBAHA.113.303027" pmid="24458708" pmcid="PMC4104778" count="1"><sup>18</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>This method has previously been applied in patients with FCS, in whom a median LPL activity of 33.3 mU/L (95% confidence interval, 28.5-41.3) was established for normotriglyceridemic (NTG) subjects (<citation rid="r19" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.bbrep.2025.102245" pmid="41542171" pmcid="PMC12803793" count="1"><sup>19</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>The intra-assay coefficient of variation was 5.1%, whereas the inter-assay coefficient of variation was 13.2%. <sentence_start/>Given the complexity of the assay, these values are considered acceptable. <sentence_start/>The calculated limit of detection was 0.144 mIU, and the limit of quantification was 1.83 mIU. <sentence_start/>A value of 6.6 mIU corresponds to 20% of normal activity. <sentence_start/>Therefore, LPL activity below this threshold is supportive of a diagnosis of FCS.

A functional assay was also performed. <sentence_start/>Two substrates were prepared, one of which included 10% v/v normolipemic human serum, heat-inactivated at 56 °C for 30 minutes and used as a source of exogenous cofactors, including ApoC-II and ApoA5. <sentence_start/>The <italic toggle="yes">in vitro</italic> assay was used to evaluate potential cofactor deficiency (<citation rid="r18" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1161/ATVBAHA.113.303027" pmid="24458708" pmcid="PMC4104778" count="1"><sup>18</sup></citation>).
<italic toggle="yes">In silico</italic> evaluation of APOA5-LPL: <italic toggle="yes">GPIHBP1</italic> interactions

Because no crystal structure is available for human <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic>, its structure was obtained from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (ID: ) and used as a template. <sentence_start/>Structural modeling of the identified variant was performed using SWISS-MODEL, followed by energy minimization with SwissPDB Viewer (<citation rid="r20" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3389/fcvm.2022.926631" pmid="35911520" pmcid="PMC9329559" count="1"><sup>20</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Energy-minimized models of both the native and mutant <italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic> proteins, along with the LPL-<italic toggle="yes">Gpihbp1</italic> complex (PDB ID: 6E7K), were uploaded to the HDOCK server, which calculates docking scores; lower scores indicate more favorable binding interactions (<citation rid="r21" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ygeno.2023.110567" pmid="36690263" count="1"><sup>21</sup></citation>).
Statistical analysis

Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages, while continuous variables were described using mean, standard deviation, median, and range (minimum-maximum). <sentence_start/>Results are presented as mean values with their corresponding standard errors. <sentence_start/>Comparisons between groups were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the Chi-square test, as appropriate. <sentence_start/>Statistical analyses were conducted using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences software (v. 25.0). <sentence_start/>A <italic toggle="yes">p</italic>-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS

<bold>Table 1</bold> summarizes the clinical and biochemical characteristics of the patients. <sentence_start/>All had a Moulin score ≥10 and a history of recurrent pancreatitis. <sentence_start/>The patients were unrelated and from different regions of Colombia. <sentence_start/>All carried the same homozygous variant in the <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> gene: c.694T>C; p.(Ser232Pro). <sentence_start/>This missense variant, located in exon 3, results from a T-to-C substitution at nucleotide position 694, leading to a serine-to-proline substitution at amino acid position 232. <sentence_start/>To date, it has been classified as a variant of uncertain significance (<citation rid="r9" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2023.08.003" pmid="37586912" count="1"><sup>9</sup></citation>).
LPL activity and functional assay

LPL activity for six patients are shown in <bold>Figure 1</bold>, along with the results of the <italic toggle="yes">in vitro</italic> functional assay. <sentence_start/>In all cases, LPL activity was below 20% of that observed in NTG controls. <sentence_start/>The <italic toggle="yes">in vitro</italic> assay, which included the addition of normal serum as a source of key cofactors (i.e., <italic toggle="yes">ApoC-II</italic> <italic toggle="yes">and ApoA5</italic>), demonstrated restoration of LPL activity to normal levels in all cases. <sentence_start/>These findings suggest that LPL function was preserved in the presence of functional <italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic> (<bold>Table 1</bold>). <sentence_start/>In four patients, samples could not be collected in time for shipment to Argentina for LPL activity analysis. <sentence_start/>No differences were observed between patients with and without LPL activity measurements in terms of diabetes status, history of pancreatitis, or lipid parameters, confirming the severity of the novel <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant.
Figure 1.

LPL activity levels before and after the addition of activator serum. <sentence_start/>The dotted line indicates 20% of the median LPL activity observed in NTG controls. <sentence_start/>Statistical comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
DISCUSSION

This study describes ten patients carrying a novel homozygous <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant, initially classified as a variant of uncertain significance. <sentence_start/>In patients with high clinical suspicion scores and markedly reduced LPL activity, these findings provide support for reclassifying this variant as likely pathogenic. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic> contains several functional domains: a signal peptide, an N-terminal hydrophilic domain, a lipid droplet-binding domain, a positively charged <italic toggle="yes">Gpihbp1</italic>-interacting domain, and a C-terminal hydrophobic (lipid-binding domain) (<citation rid="r11" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1097/01.mol.0000217892.00618.54" pmid="16531747" count="1"><sup>11</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Molecular analysis identified the homozygous variant : c.694T>C; p.(Ser232Pro), located in exon 3. <sentence_start/>This substitution impairs the interaction between <italic toggle="yes">ApoA5</italic> and <italic toggle="yes">Gpihbp1</italic>. <sentence_start/>The introduction of a proline residue induces local conformational rigidity, altering the spatial orientation of residues critical for <italic toggle="yes">GPIHBP1</italic> recognition. <sentence_start/>In addition, substitution of a polar serine with proline may affect binding affinity and kinetics of the <italic toggle="yes">ApoA5-Gplhbp1</italic> interaction, and its role in facilitating LPL-mediated TG lipolysis (<citation rid="r22" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1194/jlr.M031195" pmid="23307945" pmcid="PMC3617940" count="1"><sup>22</sup></citation>).

At least 118 definite or likely disease-causing variants in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> have been reported in the literature and databases, and are associated with FCS, hypertriglyceridemia, and atherosclerotic disease. <sentence_start/>Even minor alterations in the protein may impair its lipid-binding properties. <sentence_start/>The remaining three pathogenic LOF variants in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> could be associated with substantial functional impairment (<citation rid="r22" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1194/jlr.M031195" pmid="23307945" pmcid="PMC3617940" count="1"><sup>22</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>The variant identified (<italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic>: c.694T>C; p.Ser232Pro) likely disrupts Gpihbp1 interaction, similar to other pathogenic variants such as p.Ser232_Leu235del and p.Leu253Pro, resulting in impaired very low-density lipoprotein secretion and reduced LPL activity (<citation rid="r12" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1161/01.ATV.0000153087.36428.dd" pmid="15591215" count="1"><sup>12</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>No evidence of a dominant-negative effect has been reported for p.Ser232Pro. <sentence_start/>In previously reported cases (<citation rid="r9" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2023.08.003" pmid="37586912" count="1"><sup>9</sup></citation>), the variant showed a recessive pattern of inheritance, and heterozygous carriers exhibited normal or mildly elevated TG levels. <sentence_start/>These observations are consistent with a LOF mechanism, likely driven by impairment of the ApoA5-Gplhbp1 interaction.

Although the findings provide strong evidence for a deleterious effect of the <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> c.694T>C (p.Ser232Pro) variant, the current classification as likely pathogenic is based on ACMG/AMP criteria that do not yet meet the threshold for pathogenicity. <sentence_start/>The study shows markedly reduced LPL activity (<20% of normal), with restoration upon addition of exogenous ApoA5, supporting a LOF mechanism. <sentence_start/>However, ACMG/AMP guidelines require either multiple independent functional studies or well-validated assays to support reclassification beyond this level (<citation rid="r13" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2015.30" pmid="25741868" pmcid="PMC4544753" count="1"><sup>13</sup></citation>).

The available genetic and functional evidence supports a LOF effect and disease association. <sentence_start/>Nonetheless, the data meet ACMG/AMP criteria for “likely pathogenic” classification. <sentence_start/>Additional independent functional studies, segregation analyses, and replication in other cohorts are necessary to support full classification as “pathogenic.” Following ACMG/AMP guidelines for variant interpretation (<citation rid="r13" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2015.30" pmid="25741868" pmcid="PMC4544753" count="1"><sup>13</sup></citation>) (ClinGen framework updates), the variant met criteria PM3 (strong), PM2 (supporting), and PP3 (supporting), and was therefore classified as “likely pathogenic.” <sentence_start/>Overall, p.Ser232Pro behaves similarly to other structurally disruptive <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variants, with pathogenicity consistent with a recessive LOF mechanism (<citation rid="r21" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ygeno.2023.110567" pmid="36690263" count="1"><sup>21</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>The clinical and functional data support the pathogenicity of this variant.

LPL activity below 20% is strongly associated with a diagnosis of FCS and with the exclusion of multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome (<citation rid="r23" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.clinbiochem.2023.02.002" pmid="36780934" count="1"><sup>23</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r24" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2024.12.020" pmid="40023744" count="1"><sup>24</sup></citation>), in combination with the Moulin score (<citation rid="r16" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2018.06.814" pmid="29980054" count="1"><sup>16</sup></citation>), and North American FCS scores (<citation rid="r25" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2024.09.008" pmid="39537503" count="1"><sup>25</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>In our cohort, LPL activity was consistently below 20% of NTG controls, supporting the pathogenicity of this variant. <sentence_start/>Genetic testing fails to provide definitive results in a substantial proportion of FCS patients, even when the Moulin and North American FCS scores scores strongly suggest a high likelihood of disease (<citation rid="r16" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2018.06.814" pmid="29980054" count="1"><sup>16</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r25" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2024.09.008" pmid="39537503" count="1"><sup>25</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>The APPROACH study reported that 21% of participants lacked identifiable genetic variants but were included based on their clinical presentation and markedly reduced LPL activity (<citation rid="r14" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2018.05.013" pmid="30318066" count="1"><sup>14</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>LPL activity below 20% is strongly associated with FCS diagnosis and supports the exclusion of multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome (<citation rid="r23" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.clinbiochem.2023.02.002" pmid="36780934" count="1"><sup>23</sup></citation>,<citation rid="r24" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2024.12.020" pmid="40023744" count="1"><sup>24</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>In our cohort, LPL activity was consistently below 20% of NTG controls, supporting the pathogenicity of this variant. <sentence_start/>Although LPL activity testing is complex and not widely available, it is valuable in cases with inconclusive genetic results or unclear differentiation between FCS and multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome. <sentence_start/>We recently reported a case of a pregnant patient with severe hypertriglyceridemia (6900 mg/dL) and a history of pancreatitis (<citation rid="r24" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.jacl.2024.12.020" pmid="40023744" count="1"><sup>24</sup></citation>). <sentence_start/>Genetic testing identified a heterozygous <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant (c.111delC; p.Asp37Glufs*20), classified as likely pathogenic. <sentence_start/>LPL activity was below 20% (9.6%), increasing to 31.2% after addition of activator serum, supporting a diagnosis of FCS and reclassification of the variant.

In conclusion, our findings showed that rare variants in <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> play a critical role in the pathophysiology of FCS. <sentence_start/>In this study, we documented reduced LPL activity, supporting the diagnosis and demonstrating the functional impact of the <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant. <sentence_start/>We propose a founder effect for this novel homozygous <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variant, which has also been reported in a prior case classified as a variant of uncertain significance. <sentence_start/>Novel <italic toggle="yes">APOA5</italic> variants are likely to be reclassified as pathogenic and LPL activity data continue to accumulate.

<bold>Limitations:</bold> although the cohort was well-characterized, the sample size was limited (n = 10), which was expected given the extremely low prevalence of FCS (approximately 1 in 1,000,000) and the description of a novel variant. <sentence_start/>In addition, no <italic toggle="yes">in vitro</italic> functional studies (e.g., Gpihbp1 binding assays) were performed to directly assess the mechanistic impact of the variant.

<bold>Ethical considerations:</bold> the study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Faculty of Pharmacy and Biochemistry, University of Buenos Aires (RESCD-2021-842-E-UBA-DCT_FFYB). <sentence_start/>All investigations were conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki. <sentence_start/>Written informed consent was obtained from all participants prior to DNA collection, blood sampling, and administration of heparin for post-heparin LPL activity analysis.
